clue.text: A tray's in use should be clean

indicators.note: putting letters to use here means working them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, with the S of the contraction kept
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice that any tray brought into service ought to be spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use' is the anagram signal: the letters of A TRAY'S IN are rearranged; 'should be' only links fodder to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanitary describes conditions that are hygienic and free from dirt.

clue.text: Priest playing in a band

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are messing about and rearranging themselves

explanation.surface: A clergyman performs as a member of a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals an anagram of PRIEST; 'band' is a strip of colour, not musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow strip of colour, a band across a surface.

clue.text: Spicy stuff for the head girl!

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
Meg is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An exclamation about something hot and spicy reserved for the school's head girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head girl' looks like a school prefect; it splits into the head (NUT) and a girl (MEG).
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is a fragrant seed ground as a cooking spice.

clue.text: Lure coloured salesman inside

indicators.note: inside places the salesman within the word for coloured

parts.note: tan is a brownish colour, so to be coloured can be tanned or tan
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: Tempting a sun-browned travelling salesman indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Trepan is an old verb meaning to ensnare or entrap someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To trepan, in archaic usage, is to trap or entice someone by trickery.

clue.text: Share with a colleague in a reasonable way

parts.note: to ration is to share out in fixed portions
an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: Dividing things fairly with a co-worker in a sensible manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The scanned text breaks 'reasonable' into 'areas enable'; the definition is 'in a reasonable way'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting rationally means acting logically, guided by sound judgement.

clue.text: A gift of ancient coin

definitions.meaning: a unit of weight and money in the ancient Greek and Roman world

explanation.surface: Someone's present turns out to be an old piece of currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a natural aptitude and an old weight of silver or gold used as money, as in the biblical parable.

clue.text: Out-moded gun-put in a silencer

indicators.note: in places the word for put inside the silencer

parts.note: a mute is a device that deadens sound
to set is to put or place

explanation.surface: Instructions for fitting a silencer to an obsolete firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: An amusette was a light field cannon of the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: The amusette was a small light cannon long since out of service, so an obsolete firearm.

clue.text: New pieces almost all outstanding

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh order
almost means the word all is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before the trim

explanation.surface: Fresh components nearly all of excellent quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' signals an anagram of PIECES, giving ESPECI; 'almost all' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial means exceptional or particular, standing out from the ordinary.

clue.text: Restrained note the revolutionary's written

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written
a red is a communist or revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel's handwritten message, perhaps penned in captivity.
explanation.definitionFit: Tethered means tied up on a rope or chain, so held back from moving freely.

clue.text: Withdraws engineers before doctors

indicators.note: before puts the engineers first in the answer

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a doctor treats patients

explanation.surface: A military unit pulls back while medics move up behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctors' is a verb here, giving TREATS rather than DRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Retreats is a verb for pulling back or moving away from a position.

clue.text: Figure it's a little dog to stroke

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
to pet an animal is to stroke it

explanation.surface: Someone calls a small dog a figure to be stroked.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet is a small model figure moved by strings or a hand.

clue.text: The hunter taking part rode badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are ridden poorly into a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A huntsman joined the meet but rode poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' signals an anagram of PART RODE.
explanation.definitionFit: A predator is an animal that hunts and kills others for food.

clue.text: Sorry about a key on the computer keyboard which was meant to SAVE

indicators.note: about places the word for sorry around the key

parts.note: to rue something is to be sorry for it

parts.words: a key on the computer keyboard
parts.note: Esc is the escape key at the top left of a keyboard

explanation.surface: Regret at hitting the wrong key when meaning to save a file.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised SAVE suggests the computer command but is just the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue is to save someone from danger.

clue.text: The timekeeper has little help

parts.note: minute means very small
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: An official in charge of time gets only a small assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timekeeper' suggests an official; it is a pointer on a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The longer pointer on a clock face marks the minutes, so it keeps time.

clue.text: The scholar with sense standing in front of class is a trier

indicators.note: standing in front of places the sense before the class in the answer

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a scholar
the gist is the general sense of something
rate means class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A sensible academic standing before pupils is put in the role of judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trier' here means one who tries cases in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate hears and decides court cases, so is someone who tries offenders.

clue.text: A point a lawless individual made sound

parts.note: S is south, a point of the compass
a pirate is a sea robber outside the law

explanation.surface: A buccaneer makes a valid argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' here is a verb: to aspirate is to pronounce with an audible breath, as the h in 'hat'.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics, to aspirate a consonant is to voice it with a puff of breath.

clue.text: We hear, Anna and Liza meet a guy who's resolved

indicators.note: we hear says the two names are spoken and the sound written down

parts.note: two girls' names, said together

explanation.surface: Two women are introduced to a determined man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' here means broke something down into parts, not determined.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has resolved a problem into its parts has examined it closely, which is what an analyst does.

clue.text: Ranges in order people's in incomes

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are set in a new sequence

explanation.surface: A list putting salary bands in sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' signals an anagram of RANGES IN; the scan splits 'incomes' in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money people are paid for their work.

clue.text: He'll get the sack at Christmas

definitions.text: He'll get the sack at Christmas

parts.words: He'll get the sack at Christmas
parts.note: sounds like a worker dismissed over the holidays, but describes the bearded gift-bringer who carries a bag of presents

explanation.surface: A worker fears dismissal over the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive gift-bringer famously carries a sack of toys on Christmas Eve.

clue.text: The very old see about nothing

indicators.note: about means the word see goes around nothing

parts.note: taken as written
nil means nothing, as in a football score

explanation.surface: Elderly people pay attention to trivial matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The very old' must stand as an adjective here: senile, as of the very old.
explanation.definitionFit: Senile describes the frailty of extreme old age.

clue.text: Taste the French in foies gras, for example

indicators.note: in puts the French article within the word for foie gras

parts.note: foie gras is a kind of pâté, a meat paste
la is the French for 'the' (feminine)

explanation.surface: Sampling the French way with goose liver.
explanation.definitionFit: The palate is one's sense of taste, as in a refined palate.

clue.text: Failing and fed-up with failing, etc.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word fed is read from bottom to top
failing suggests the letters break down into a new order

explanation.surface: Bored and exasperated by repeated breakdowns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses FED to DEF and the second 'failing' scrambles ETC to ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A defect is a fault or shortcoming, a failing.

clue.text: Where one's to settle!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, and 's adds S
to land is to come down and settle

explanation.surface: A pointed suggestion of where someone should make a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of land in water is a place one may come to rest and live, a castaway's home.

clue.text: Left always ahead of time -such an advantage

indicators.note: ahead of puts always before time in the answer

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Getting away early always gives a head start.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is the power or edge gained to influence a situation.

clue.text: Acquiesce when told to go

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'
someone sent away has been told to go

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to leave once ordered out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acquiesce' is a noun use here: an assent is an act of acquiescing, or read 'assent' as the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to agree or give in to a proposal.

clue.text: Prepared for a soaking?

parts.note: reads like someone braced for rain, but describes the seasoned liquid a cook makes to steep meat in

explanation.surface: Someone expects to get drenched.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook makes this seasoned liquid so that food can steep in it before cooking.

clue.text: Serge's get-up is way out!

indicators.note: a get-up is an outfit, so the cloth's letters are dressed in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, with the S kept

explanation.surface: A man's outfit is outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way out' looks like slang for outlandish; it is the definition, an exit.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit, a means of leaving a place.

clue.text: A sticker for a preservationist group — about 500 present

indicators.note: about places the article and the group around the other letters

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, the British body that preserves historic houses
D is the Roman numeral for 500
here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: A supporter of a heritage society, about five hundred of them attending.
explanation.walkthrough: A HERE NT wraps D: A and NT go around D plus HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower who sticks to a cause or party.
